content:
Looking for commercial dishwasher manufacturers in China? Start with the customers you sell to. A café equipment dealer needs a different range from an importer supplying hotel wash-up lines. Veetsan, DAVOSA, Axewood and PHEDATON offer useful starting points; the list below also covers broader kitchen manufacturers and international brands with production in China. For a first order, we would narrow the choice to a few models, compare the same configuration and settle parts support before adding your logo. DDNZ combines manufacturing and trade to offer factory-price supply and model-specific low-MOQ trials, with kitchen layout support when the machine is part of a complete project.

Send DDNZ your destination, customer type and trial quantities. A product photo or an existing quotation is enough to start.

1. Ten manufacturers to compare

This shortlist is grouped around buying needs: dishwasher ranges first, broader kitchen packages next, then international brand channels. The order is a starting point for enquiries, rather than a quality league table.

ManufacturerProduct range to examineFirst question for your quotation
VeetsanUndercounter, hood and conveyor machinesWhich electrical version and export support apply?
DAVOSAGlasswashers, hood, rack and flight machinesWhat changes between standard supply and OEM?
AxewoodHood, rack-conveyor and flight machinesWhat is included with the machine and tabling?
PHEDATONHood, rack-conveyor and flight machinesCan the wash-up line fit the project drawing?
LAIKEER / HaobaHood, channel and long-line machinesCan it demonstrate cleaning with your customers’ dishes?
YongtuoGlasswashers, hood, basket and flight machinesWhich range matches the operation and local service skills?
CHINENGHood and conveyor machines; wider kitchen rangeCan the dishwasher and surrounding equipment be itemised?
SHINELONGDishwashers within a complete kitchen offeringWho manufactures and services the quoted model?
HOBART ChinaUndercounter, hood, conveyor and utensil machinesIs the model available through your destination’s channel?
MEIKO ChinaUndercounter and larger warewashing systemsWhat are the model’s production origin and local support terms?

Read the machines from the loading side: an undercounter unit takes a rack through the front door; a hood machine lifts its cover so a rack can slide across the worktables; a conveyor machine moves the load through successive washing sections. Choose the loading method before comparing capacity.

2. Where each manufacturer fits your buying brief

1. Veetsan — a focused warewashing range. Veetsan’s range runs from compact glass and dishwashing machines to larger conveyor systems. It is worth examining when you want a dealer range within one specialist brand. Ask for the model-specific installation sheet and export parts route before choosing the machines you will stock.

2. DAVOSA — an OEM discussion. Shenzhen DAVOSA manufactures commercial dishwashers and offers OEM/ODM services. Its range includes glasswashers, hood and conveyor machines. Separate the standard-machine order from logo, control-panel language and packaging changes. Ask which customisations require a larger production quantity and whether replacement controls retain the same part numbers.

3. Axewood — dishwashing alongside cooking equipment. Guangzhou Axewood manufactures dishwashers and other commercial kitchen equipment. Its catalogue includes hood, rack-conveyor and flight machines. For a mixed kitchen order, request a separate dishwasher schedule covering tables, racks, dosing and drainage, so the attractive package price can be checked item by item.

4. PHEDATON — project-sized washing lines. PHEDATON offers hood, rack-conveyor, flight and ultrasonic equipment, with customisation around kitchen measurements. Its T60 is one hood-type reference to investigate. Send a measured drawing early, including the dirty-dish arrival point and clean-rack exit. Ask for the actual loading direction and service access on the proposed layout.

5. LAIKEER / Haoba — restaurant and canteen washing. Shandong Boxing County Haoba Washing Equipment markets LAIKEER machines, including hood, channel and long-line categories. For buyers serving kitchens with different bowls, plates and food residues, send photographs of that tableware. Request a demonstration using a comparable load and agree the result you will accept.

6. Yongtuo — a broad cleaning-equipment range. Henan Yongtuo lists undercounter glasswashers, hood, basket and flight machines alongside specialist cleaning equipment. Keep your enquiry specific: washing drinking glasses and handling a canteen’s dirty returns are different jobs. Choose the machine category first, then ask for the service manual and parts schedule for that exact model.

7. CHINENG — a wider kitchen assortment. CHINENG lists hood, rack-conveyor and flight dishwashers alongside cooking and other kitchen equipment. This gives wholesalers another range to compare for mixed orders. Put each model, electrical version and accessory on its own quotation line; request the producing factory’s details for the machines selected.

8. SHINELONG — complete kitchen procurement. Guangzhou SHINELONG offers kitchen planning and equipment manufacturing, with dishwashers in its product range. Consider it when the purchase includes the wash-up area and other kitchen zones. For the dishwasher itself, confirm the legal manufacturer, parts source and warranty contact instead of assuming the whole package has one service arrangement.

9. HOBART China — a branded supply route. HOBART is an international brand with manufacturing in Tianjin and an extensive warewashing range. Check the destination’s sales channel, the exact production origin and warranty eligibility. A China factory location alone does not establish permission to resell a model in every country or availability for private labelling.

10. MEIKO China — another branded comparison. MEIKO is a German-origin manufacturer with production in China as well as other countries. Its portfolio covers compact machines and larger wash-up systems. Specify the model and market when comparing offers, and obtain the local installation and parts-support terms. Do not assume every MEIKO model is made in China.

3. Compare the complete factory-price configuration

Suppose two hood dishwashers look almost identical. One quotation includes dosing pumps, a drain pump and racks; the other prices these separately. Comparing only the machine total will tell you little about your resale margin.

Use one quotation sheet for the shortlisted models:

Confirm togetherWhy the importer needs it
Model, rack size, usable opening and loading directionTo fit customers’ tableware and wash-up layout
Voltage, frequency, phase, total load and water requirementsTo have the destination’s installer check site compatibility
Dosing, rinse heating, drainage, tables and racksTo compare the same delivered scope
Packing, shipping terms, documents and spare-parts packageTo build a meaningful landed-cost estimate

Ask for applicable electrical-safety documentation for the destination and the exact model. IEC 60335-2-58 addresses commercial electric dishwashing machines; a reference to the standard is not a substitute for the model’s conformity documents. Our Gulf dishwasher selection guide goes further into water, heating and working output.

4. Start small, but settle parts and support first

For a trial, we would concentrate on a small number of models that your customers can use and your technicians can maintain. Ask DDNZ for low-MOQ options on standard configurations, with custom branding priced separately. The available quantity and factory price must be confirmed against the selected model, electrical version and packing.

Before paying, request an exploded parts list and price the proposed starter spares: seals, wash-arm components, filters, switches and model-specific electrical parts. Agree which items your technician can replace, what evidence a warranty claim needs, who pays freight and whether labour is covered. A generic “one-year warranty” leaves too much unresolved.

DDNZ’s integrated manufacturing-and-trade approach connects the equipment offer with the kitchen plan, trial order and agreed production visibility. For a complete wash-up station, send the floor plan; for stock, send the models and quantities. We can work through the specification and quotation with you before you commit to a wider range. Keep the confirmed part numbers with each order using the approach in our commercial kitchen spare-parts guide.

Questions before your first wholesale order

Which manufacturer should a new importer contact first?

Start with the machine type your customers already request. For OEM, include DAVOSA in the comparison; for a specialist branded range, examine Veetsan. Send DDNZ your customer type and destination so we can narrow the supply brief before discussing trial quantities.

Can I trial a small quantity at a factory price?

Ask for a standard-model trial first. DDNZ can propose model-specific low-MOQ options; logo changes, packaging and electrical customisation need separate confirmation. Compare the written configuration and shipping terms, rather than treating a small-order unit price as an all-in cost.

What should I request for after-sales support?

Request the exact model’s parts list, wiring diagram, service instructions and warranty procedure before ordering. Name the local technician or service partner who will handle installation and repairs, and agree the price and freight responsibility for replacement parts.

Can DDNZ help if I only have a kitchen drawing?

Yes. Send the floor plan, menu or operation type, destination and expected busy-service load. We can start with the wash-up layout and equipment plan, then develop the purchasing list and factory-price supply options.

Send your shortlist or kitchen plan to DDNZ

Contact DDNZ for a dishwasher trial-order proposal. Include your company, destination country and city, machine type, electrical supply and quantities. Attach the kitchen drawing or product references, and tell us whether you need your own branding and a starter spare-parts package.
